evidence.estrutura: Robinson was an economist rather than a constitutional theorist. No reliable territorial centralization doctrine is established.
evidence.representacao: Her political sympathies were left-wing and at times admiring of socialist experiments, but her economics does not provide a clear electoral-regime theory. Keep representation moderate pending direct political writings.
evidence.poder: Her economic work criticizes monopoly power and exploitation, supporting skepticism toward concentrated private economic power. This does not automatically establish a civil-liberty versus security position.
evidence.imigracao: No reliable immigration doctrine is central to her work. Keep moderate.
evidence.diplomacia: She engaged internationally with development and socialist economies but was not primarily a diplomacy theorist. Keep moderate.
evidence.intervencao: No stable military-intervention doctrine is established. Her anti-imperialist sympathies suggest restraint toward great-power intervention.
evidence.economia: As a central Keynesian and later heterodox economist critical of orthodox capitalism, Robinson strongly supports a large public role, demand management and alternatives to laissez-faire economics.
evidence.controle: Her Keynesian and socialist sympathies support substantial macroeconomic planning and public coordination, though her work is not a blueprint for total command planning.
evidence.comercio: Her development economics criticized simplistic free-trade orthodoxy and unequal international economic relations, supporting managed trade rather than pure laissez-faire globalism.
evidence.religiao: Her economics and public thought are secular rather than grounded in religious authority.
evidence.moral: Her politics were egalitarian and anti-imperialist, but she was not primarily a theorist of modern cultural issues. Use moderate progressive placement.
evidence.tecnologia: Her growth and capital theory engages industrial development positively; she was not anti-technology. Use a moderately technophile development-oriented position.
